label: Adaptive Flesh
description:
“The body is our general medium for having a world.”
 Maurice Merleau-Ponty, Phenomenology of Perception

If the body is the medium through which the world is perceived and experienced, what happens when that world loses its coherence?

Exteneral is an ongoing research project exploring body architectures as aesthetic and functional responses to forced evolution.

It begins with an uncomfortable proposition: adaptation is never innocent. A body redesigned for survival exists somewhere between evolution and violence. What appears as enhancement from the outside may be experienced as an invasion from within.

At the centre of the project is this suspended state: the vulnerable interval in which the former anatomy can no longer hold, while the next has not yet stabilised.

Mutation is no longer a deviation from the system. It becomes the system itself.
descriptionMobile:
“The body is our general medium for having a world.”
Maurice Merleau-Ponty, Phenomenology of Perception

Exteneral explores body architectures as aesthetic and functional responses to forced evolution.

It begins with an uncomfortable proposition: adaptation is never innocent. A body redesigned for survival exists between evolution and violence. Anatomies shift, functions change, and new structures emerge to inhabit unfamiliar conditions. What appears as enhancement from the outside may be felt as invasion from within.

At its centre is a suspended state: the moment in which the former anatomy can no longer hold, while the next has not stabilised. 

Mutation is no longer a deviation from the system; it becomes the system itself.
